title: Fourier-Domain Optical Coherence Tomographic Assessment of Changes in the Schlemm’s Canal of Nonglaucomatous Subjects After Keratoplasty

groups.description: Penetrating keratoplasty in nonglaucomatous eyes; indications (Table 1): corneal stromal dystrophies, keratoconus, corneal leucoma, corneal graft failure (5 repeat grafts reported as an indication) and endothelial decompensation. The surgery types are PK, DALK and triple surgery (PK + ECCE + IOL); cataract extraction belongs to the triple-surgery type only, so this group had none.

Deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty; indications (Table 1): keratoconus, corneal leucoma, corneal stromal dystrophies. Cataract extraction belongs to the triple-surgery type only, so this group had none.

Triple surgery: penetrating keratoplasty with extracapsular cataract extraction and intraocular lens implantation in the same operation; indications (Table 1): corneal leucoma, corneal stromal dystrophies, endothelial decompensation.

notes: Prospective comparative observational study (August 2018 to December 2020) of 66 nonglaucomatous eyes of 66 patients; examinations preoperatively and 1 day and 1 week after surgery; preoperative exclusions only (concurrent glaucoma, ocular trauma, high axial myopia, keratoconus with acute hydrops); no minimum follow-up criterion.
IOP and Schlemm's canal parameters (Tables 2, 3) are tabulated: notes only.
